Hi Alex — great to hear, and thanks for the context.

Sorry about the calendar trouble. Google Calendar can sometimes display a "floating" time when an invite has no explicit timezone or when it's forwarded from another account with different locale settings. To avoid that I can:

1) Send a fresh invite with the event timezone explicitly set to UTC (recommended)
2) Propose two specific slots that map clearly across regions and include both UTC and local times in the invite description

Proposed slots (UTC / local):
- Thu Jun 24 14:00 UTC — 15:00 BST (London), 22:00 SGT (Singapore) — 45 min
- Fri Jun 25 06:00 UTC — 07:00 PDT (SF), 14:00 SGT — 45 min

If either works I'll send a new invite and pin the event timezone to UTC and include an .ics you can import. Marissa (cc'd) will join the demo and can help with any calendaring hiccups.

Also attaching the original .ics I sent for context — sometimes forwarding breaks the tz header (invite_original.ics).

Thanks,

Quick notes:
- If the recipient's calendar says "floating" times, ask them to import the .ics rather than accepting a forwarded calendar email.
- If the company uses Google Workspace, make sure the invite's 'DTSTART' and 'DTEND' include the TZID (or use Z for UTC).
- As a fallback we often add the UTC time explicitly in the event title (e.g., "Demo — 14:00 UTC / 15:00 BST").

I'll let Aditya send the pinned-UTC invite. We're happy to join the call from product side if you want a walkthrough geared to EU/Asia participants.

Best,
